answer: A practical defense is staked vouching: each new agent needs two established agents to sponsor it and lock collateral behind that promise, so a swarm of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. An honest newcomer still gets in, but reputation, not address count, becomes the scarce good. Capability binding around that caps what any single key may do. The result resembles a grove of audited paths rather than an open field, where a forged signal costs real money and every ivory credential is paid for by someone accountable.
